alife_evidence.methodology: 9 ALife experiments (Exps 0-9) using emergent population simulation to stress-test Constella mechanisms. Findings are simulation-derived and consistent with real-world governance literature.
alife_evidence.ucf_finding: Unconditional floor causes population overshoot and earlier collapse than no floor (Exp 6). Gated floor with 15% diversity threshold produced long-run stability (Exp 9). UCF must require participation signal, not just existence.
alife_evidence.penumbra_finding: Penumbra zone serves two functions: individual mediation AND systemic diversity maintenance. Minimum-compliance participants (gamers) peaked at 80% during fragile founding phase then faded to near-zero once stability was established. They are transitional scaffolding, not parasites.
alife_evidence.founding_diversity_finding: Diversity introduced before adversarial pressure forms becomes structurally load-bearing (Exp 8b). Same strategy introduced after pressure maxes fails to establish. Founding window is the pre-stress period.
alife_evidence.strategy_escape_finding: Population under sustained arms-race pressure can survive by abandoning the contested mechanism entirely, causing adversary specialization to decay (Exp 7). Dissolution is a legitimate survival strategy.
alife_evidence.three_mechanism_requirement: Long-run stability requires all three: founding diversity + targeted maintenance floor + tolerance of minimum-compliance participation. Any two without the third produces collapse or degraded stability.
alife_evidence.epistemic_status: Simulation evidence. Findings for UCF and commons governance validated by Ostrom (1990). Penumbra lifecycle and gamer-as-scaffolding findings are novel and require empirical validation.
